classification.difficultyReason: Find each midpoint and perpendicular gradient, form the two bisector equations, then solve their explicitly requested intersection using routine linked methods.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of:

answer.short:
$y=-\frac{5}{6}x+\frac{139}{12}$.

Use the midpoint of $AB$ and the negative reciprocal of its gradient.
answer.worked:
The midpoint of $AB$ is
$$M=\left(\frac{3+8}{2},\frac{4+10}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{11}{2},7\right).$$
$$\begin{align*}m_{AB}&=\frac{10-4}{8-3}\\m_{AB}&=\frac65\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular bisector has gradient $-\frac56$ and passes through $M$.
$$\begin{align*}y-7&=-\frac56\left(x-\frac{11}{2}\right)\\12y-84&=-10x+55\\12y&=-10x+139\\y&=-\frac56x+\frac{139}{12}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$y=-\frac{3}{11}x+\frac{69}{11}$.

Use the midpoint of $BC$ and the negative reciprocal of its gradient.
answer.worked:
The midpoint of $BC$ is
$$N=\left(\frac{8+5}{2},\frac{10+(-1)}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{13}{2},\frac92\right).$$
$$\begin{align*}m_{BC}&=\frac{-1-10}{5-8}\\m_{BC}&=\frac{11}{3}\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular bisector has gradient $-\frac{3}{11}$ and passes through $N$.
$$\begin{align*}y-\frac92&=-\frac{3}{11}\left(x-\frac{13}{2}\right)\\22y-99&=-6x+39\\22y&=-6x+138\\y&=-\frac{3}{11}x+\frac{69}{11}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point of intersection of the two perpendicular bisectors.

answer.short:
$\left(\frac{701}{74},\frac{273}{74}\right)$.

Solve the two perpendicular-bisector equations simultaneously.
answer.worked:
At the intersection, the two expressions for $y$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}-\frac56x+\frac{139}{12}&=-\frac{3}{11}x+\frac{69}{11}\\-110x+1529&=-36x+828\\74x&=701\\x&=\frac{701}{74}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the perpendicular bisector of $BC$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac{3}{11}\left(\frac{701}{74}\right)+\frac{69}{11}\\y&=\frac{-2103+5106}{814}\\y&=\frac{273}{74}\end{align*}$$
Check in the equivalent equations from part a:
$$\begin{align*}10\left(\frac{701}{74}\right)+12\left(\frac{273}{74}\right)&=139\\6\left(\frac{701}{74}\right)+22\left(\frac{273}{74}\right)&=138\end{align*}$$
The point of intersection is $\left(\frac{701}{74},\frac{273}{74}\right)$.
